$comment: Source of truth for 'Add with icons to your AI tool' (site/data/integrations.js via forge/tools/site-integrations.mjs) and for packages/cli/src/init.mjs. Every fact is from the tool's official docs (see sources) as of `verified`. Re-check before changing; never guess a command. `mcp.json` is pretty-printed into mcp.snippet by the generator; deeplinks are computed from `servers`.
name: withicons

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.blurb: Skill in .claude/skills plus the MCP server, so Claude Code searches icons by meaning and pastes the right import.

steps.title: One command
steps.text: Run in your project. It copies the skill to .claude/skills/with-icons/ and adds the server to .mcp.json. Add --global for every project.

steps.title: Or add the server with Claude Code's own CLI
steps.text: Remote, no install. Use --scope user for all projects or --scope project to share it through .mcp.json.
steps.code: claude mcp add --transport http withicons https://withicons.com/mcp

steps.title: Run it locally instead
steps.text: The same server over stdio (Node 18+).
steps.code: claude mcp add --transport stdio withicons -- npx -y @withicons/mcp

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Type /mcp in Claude Code to see the withicons tools, and ask for "an icon for deleting things, in React".

tools.name: OpenAI Codex
tools.blurb: For the Codex CLI, IDE extension and app: the skill in .agents/skills and the server in config.toml.

steps.title: One command
steps.text: Copies the skill to .agents/skills/with-icons/ and adds [mcp_servers.withicons] to .codex/config.toml (Codex reads project config in trusted projects). Add --global to use ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.agents/skills.

steps.title: Or use the Codex CLI
steps.text: Streamable HTTP, no install.

steps.title: Run it locally instead
steps.text: stdio via npx (Node 18+).

steps.title: IDE extension
steps.text: The CLI, IDE extension and app share config.toml. In the extension: gear menu > MCP servers > Add server > Streamable HTTP, then restart the extension.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.blurb: One click adds the server to Cursor. The skill goes in .agents/skills, which Cursor loads automatically.

steps.title: One click
steps.text: Use the Add to Cursor button. Cursor opens and asks you to confirm the withicons server.

steps.title: Or one command
steps.text: Copies the skill to .agents/skills/with-icons/ and adds the server to .cursor/mcp.json. Add --global for ~/.cursor/mcp.json.

steps.title: Or edit mcp.json yourself
steps.text: Project: .cursor/mcp.json. Everywhere: ~/.cursor/mcp.json.

tools.name: OpenCode
tools.blurb: Adds a remote MCP entry to opencode.json and the skill to .agents/skills, which OpenCode discovers on its own.

steps.title: One command
steps.text: Copies the skill to .agents/skills/with-icons/ and adds "withicons" under "mcp" in opencode.json. Add --global for ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json and ~/.agents/skills.

steps.title: Or edit opencode.json
steps.text: OpenCode merges project and global config. opencode mcp add also walks you through it interactively.

steps.title: Check
steps.text: Run opencode mcp list.

tools.name: Lovable
tools.blurb: Connect the remote server as a chat connector and import the skill from GitHub. No install.

steps.title: Add the MCP server
steps.text: Open Connectors, choose + (top right) > MCP server. Name: with icons. URL: https://withicons.com/mcp. Authentication: none. Available on all plans; each teammate connects their own.

steps.title: Add the skill (owners and admins)
steps.text: Workspace settings > Skills > Add > Import from GitHub, and paste this link. It is shared with every project in the workspace.

steps.title: Or add project knowledge
steps.text: Project settings > Knowledge (up to 10,000 characters). Paste the note below.

skill.snippet: Icons: use the "with icons" library (https://withicons.com, MIT). Read https://withicons.com/skill/SKILL.md before adding icons. Find names with the withicons MCP server (search_icons) or https://withicons.com/api/search?q=<words>; never invent an icon name. React: npm i @withicons/react, then import { Home } from '@withicons/react'. Use the line style for UI, solid for active states, and one style per region. Icon-only buttons need an aria-label.

tools.name: Claude Desktop
tools.blurb: Add the remote server as a custom connector, or run it locally from claude_desktop_config.json. Upload the skill as a zip.

steps.title: Remote connector
steps.text: Customize > Connectors > + > Add custom connector, then paste the URL. Free plans allow one custom connector.

steps.title: Or run it locally
steps.text: This command adds the npx server to claude_desktop_config.json (Claude menu > Settings > Developer > Edit Config). Quit and reopen Claude afterwards.

steps.title: Upload the skill
steps.text: Make the zip, then go to Customize > Skills > + > Create skill > Upload a skill. Code execution must be on.

tools.name: VS Code (Copilot)
tools.blurb: Install the server in one click for Copilot agent mode. The skill goes in .agents/skills, which VS Code loads.

steps.title: One click
steps.text: Use Install in VS Code. VS Code asks you to confirm and trust the server.

steps.title: Or one command
steps.text: Copies the skill to .agents/skills/with-icons/ and adds the server to .vscode/mcp.json.

steps.title: Or the VS Code CLI (user profile)
steps.text: Adds the local server to your user mcp.json.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.blurb: Windsurf is now Devin Desktop. Its Cascade agent reads MCP servers from your user mcp_config.json and skills from .agents/skills.

steps.title: One command
steps.text: Copies the skill to .agents/skills/with-icons/ and adds the server to your user mcp_config.json (~/.config/devin/, or %APPDATA%\devin\ on Windows; an existing ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json is updated too).

steps.title: Or edit mcp_config.json
steps.text: Cascade has no one-click install. Remote servers use serverUrl. Refresh the MCP list afterwards.
